title: Is Khanmigo a Dud
author: Learning Insights, AI
summary: Sal Khan's 2023 promise that AI would spark the greatest education transformation via personal tutoring has given way to reality: students simply don't use Khanmigo much. The tool is a non-event for many learners. Khan Academy is now admitting that AI works best for already-motivated students and that human teachers remain essential. The piece challenges the hype around AI tutoring and refocuses on what actually drives learning.
points: Khanmigo proved to be a non-event for students; they simply didn't use it much despite its availability.
AI tutoring works only for students who would thrive anyway; struggling students still need human teachers.
Khan Academy now emphasizes investing in human systems over expecting AI to be the transformation lever.
The biggest barrier to learning is student engagement and motivation, not access to technology.
Bold AI claims often fail to account for the reality of how students actually behave with new tools.
quotes: For a lot of students, it was a non-event. They just didn't use it much.
If students don't engage with the material enough to know what they're looking for, then an AI like Khanmigo doesn't necessarily help.
Students were not seeking out Khanmigo's help as much as we had hoped.
The platform works best for students who would thrive anyway; those who struggle still need teachers.
Khan Academy is like Brussels sprouts. Teachers and parents know it's good for kids. But kids don't always think so.” Archived from AI Learn Insights on May 2, 2026 by Tim.
